title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving primary health services to vulnerable communities affected by climatic shocks in Diinsoor district

description.narrative: ltpgtVRD aims to establish a comprehensive primary health care services project to address the urgent needs of vulnerable communities affected by climatic shocks in Diinsoor District, Somalia. The project responds to the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) 1st standard allocation for 2025. This initiative will involve operating 1 fixed health center and 1 outreach mobile clinic team, covering five villages and four Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) sites. Driven by a strong commitment to alleviate suffering and improve well-being, VRD seeks to provide essential health care assistance to the most vulnerable populations, including women, girls, boys, men, persons with special needs, and host communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtThe name of the health facility is Waberi MCH, and three other villages for the outreach program: Jameeco, Bula Xanshi and Bulo Yanye. The project targets 3 IDPs, namely: Warabow IDP, Qodqod IDP, and Eesow IDP. The project targets a total of 15,000 households for the period.lt/bgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe proposed intervention is designed to have a lasting impact, to an estimated 15,426 directly and indirectly, attending outpatient departments, 2100 pregnant women will receive antenatal care services, while the intervention targets to provide safe delivery to 1,600 pregnant mothers, Measles vaccination for 3,630 children under the age of five, a total of 180 beneficiaries will receive GVB treatment and referral cases. The project aims to reach lt/spangtltspangt27lt/spangtltspangt,000 beneficiaries for health promotion information activities. Additionally, capacity building for 35 healthcare staff and 20 Community Health Workers (CHWs) will be provided to improve the quality of services, and 20 staff will be trained on GBV/lt/spangtltspangtPSEA.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtKey services will include free outpatient consultations for common illnesses, antenatal and postnatal care, skilled delivery services, immunizations, Cholera Treatment Unit (CTU), routine vaccination services, and trauma care. Additionally, the project will address gender-based violence by integrating clinical management of rape and facilitating referrals to specialized protection centers through established pathways.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtTo ensure effective implementation, VRD will employ community health workers dedicated to active case finding, defaulter tracing, and health promotion. The project will adopt a community-based participatory approach, strengthening local capacity through training and collaboration with community health workers (CHWs) to ensure sustainability.lt/pgtltpgtVRD has established partnerships with national and international NGOs, enhancing coordination and avoiding duplication of efforts in delivering humanitarian services. The project will specifically address the needs of women, girls, boys, men, persons with disabilities, under-five children, pregnant and lactating women, the elderly, and marginalized groups affected by climate-related challenges and conflict displacement.ltbrgtWith a solid presence in Diinsoor District and positive relationships with local communities and authorities, VRD is well-positioned for successful project implementation. Our extensive experience in the region has fostered trust, enabling effective collaboration and communication with community members.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project aligns with the strategic objectives of the Somalia Needs Humanitarian Response Plan (HNRP 2025) and cluster objectives, aiming to provide safe, equitable, and dignified access to essential services and livelihoods. Moreover, it addresses protection risks related to exclusion and displacement, ensuring that the most vulnerable populations receive the support they need. We invite your support to help us make a meaningful difference in the lives of those affected in Diinsoor District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
